This Almost New 2020 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 Is for Sale, Can You Guess the Price?
9 photos
Photo: VanguardMotorSales
The S550 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 may not have an eponymous successor, which is why some believe that the company might be prepping an ultra-hot version of the S650, but let’s not forget that the Dark Horse SC exists.
As you likely know by now, the latter model takes less than three seconds to zip from zero to sixty miles per hour (0 to 97 kph), and features a 5.2-liter supercharged V8 under the hood. The mill is officially good for 795 bhp (806 ps/593 kW) and 660 pound-feet (895 Nm) of torque, and everything is channeled to the rear wheels (what else?) through a dual-clutch seven-speed Tremec automatic transmission.
How does it compare to the S550-based Ford Mustang Shelby GT500? Well, the power boost is not jaw dropping, as there is a difference of 35 hp (36 ps/26 kW ) and 33 pound-feet (45 Nm) of torque between the two, with the balance tilting in favor of the Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC (SC stands for SuperCharged). That’s because the GT500 has 760 hp (771 ps/567 kW) to play with in total, and 627 lb-ft (847 Nm) of torque from its 5.2-liter supercharged V8 engine.
Mind you, while the gap is not that significant, the performance is, or the straight-line acceleration, for that matter, which takes a little over three seconds in the Ford Mustang Shelby GT500. This model will complete the standing quarter mile in 10.7 seconds, and guess what? According to third-party estimates, that is actually one-tenth of a second faster than the Mustang Dark Horse SC. And that’s a battle worth watching.
Photo: VanguardMotorSales However, we are not here to discuss the differences and similarities between the S550-based Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 and its new-age successor, the S650 Mustang Dark Horse SC, but to put the spotlight on the GT500 pictured above. And that’s what we are doing now, because we found this example looking for a new home in the United States of America, and it is definitely worth checking out, especially if you are into this thing.
There are many reasons to love this particular pony car, and if the 760 brake horsepower available via the loud pedal is not enough to convince you, then the mileage should. That’s because this ride is said to have a mere 1,320 miles (2,125 km) under its belt, which means that it is pretty much brand new. And it likely retains that new-car smell, too. On top of that, it boasts the Carbon Fiber Track Pack, which is said to have been an $18,500 option back in the day.
As a result, it comes with the usual wheels made of the lightweight material, which measure 20 inches in diameter, and were shod in Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 tires. The carbon fiber rear wing is also part of this bundle, just like the rear-seat delete. Thus, you are looking at a veritable two-seater. The stopping power is provided by the Brembo brakes on all four corners, with ventilated rotors. And this ride features additional other goodies.
The listing also mentions stuff such as the 12-inch touchscreen infotainment system, a Bang & Olufsen premium sound system, a dual-zone climate control system, an Alcantara-wrapped steering wheel with paddle shifters, Recaro bucket seats wrapped in black Alcantara and white leather upholstery, dual illuminated vanity mirrors, and a few other bits and bobs, including the blind-spot assist.
Photo: VanguardMotorSales As the vendor says, this machine “ would make a great addition to any garage or collection, ” and who are we to say otherwise? After all, this is a great muscle car developed to take on those pesky two-door Dodge Hellcats back in the day, and it remains a fantastic daily that feels right at home at the drag strip.
Mind you, one definitely needs some deep pockets if they want to spruce up their life with a cool S550-based Ford Mustang Shelby GT500. That is because this thing can command upward of $160,000, depending on the model year, mileage, configuration, and overall condition. An earlier model year with quite a few miles under its belt can fetch roughly $100,000 in today’s used car market, and some examples have dropped below the $100K mark all the way to the $80k one, though they’re not exactly in pristine condition, to no one’s surprise.
Now that you know that the pictured Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 is a 2020 model year, as mentioned in the title, that it features the sought-after Carbon Fiber Track Pack, and that it has been kept away from the road for the most part, as it barely has any miles under its belt, how much do you think that this example costs? Unless you said $134,900, then you are wrong, as that was the asking price at the time of writing. The muscle car in question is advertised by Vanguard Motor Sales, and you can access the ad here .
